content: Striations refer to a series of ridges, furrows, or linear marks that can be observed in various contexts. In the field of glaciology, glacial striations are linear grooves or scratches on rock surfaces caused by the movement of glaciers. In geology, striations can result from geological faults, where linear marks are formed due to tectonic activity. In medicine, striations are characteristic of striated muscle tissue, such as skeletal and cardiac muscles, which exhibit a banded appearance under a microscope due to the arrangement of actin and myosin filaments. Additionally, striations can be found in certain types of glass, where they are caused by turbulent flow during the pouring or molding process of the glass material.
